results.title: Membership in $T_K$
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $K$ be a number field with ring of integers $\mathcal{O}_K$, and let $T_K$ be the set of prime ideals of $\mathcal{O}_K$ that contain $2$ and have ramification index $1$ and inertia degree $1$ over $\mathbb{Z}$. results.title: Unramified degree-one primes above $2$ in quadratic fields
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $t \ne 1$ be a squarefree integer, and let $K$ be a number field of degree $2$ over $\mathbb{Q}$ that contains an element $\alpha$ with $\alpha^2 = t$, so that $K = \mathbb{Q}(\sqrt{t})$. results.title: Eventually periodic continued fractions
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: Let $x$ be a real number with regular continued fraction $[a_0; a_1, a_2, \dots]$. The continued fraction of $x$ is eventually periodic if it does not terminate and its sequence of partial denominators $(a_n)_{n \ge 1}$, which omits the head coefficient $a_0$, is eventually periodic: there are natural numbers $p > 0$ and $n_0 \ge 1$ such that $a_{n+p} = a_n$ for every $n \ge n_0$.

results.title: Real quadratic irrationals

results.title: Ramanujan's general theta function at powers of q
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: For positive integers $i$ and $j$, $f(q^i, q^j)$ is the integer power series $\sum_{n \in \mathbb{Z}} q^{i n(n+1)/2 + j n(n-1)/2}$, that is, Ramanujan's $f(a, b) = \sum_{n \in \mathbb{Z}} a^{n(n+1)/2} b^{n(n-1)/2}$ at $a = q^i$ and $b = q^j$.

results.title: The 5-core counts
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: For a natural number $n$, $c_5(n)$ is the coefficient of $q^n$ in the integer power series $f_5^5 / f_1$, where $f_k = \prod_{m \ge 1} (1 - q^{km})$ is the Euler product. The series $f_5^5 / f_1$ is the generating function of 5-core partitions.

results.title: The φ-analog of the 5-core partition function
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: Let $\varphi(q) = \sum_{n \in \mathbb{Z}} q^{n^2}$ be Ramanujan's theta function. results.title: The ψ-analog of the 5-core partition function

results.title: Digit-sum arithmetic function
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: For a natural number $q$, $s_q$ is the arithmetic function that sends $n$ to $s_q(n)$, the sum of the digits of $n$ in base $q$. Its $k$-th Dirichlet power is the $k$-fold Dirichlet convolution $s_q^{(k)}$, so $s_q^{(1)} = s_q$ and $s_q^{(k)} = s_q * s_q^{(k-1)}$ for $k \ge 2$.

results.title: Value of the digit-sum arithmetic function
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: For natural numbers $q$ and $n$, the base-$q$ digit-sum arithmetic function $s_q$ takes at $n$ the value $s_q(n)$, the sum of the digits of $n$ in base $q$.

results.title: The second digit-sum convolution
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: For natural numbers $q$ and $n$, the Dirichlet square $s_q^{(2)} = s_q * s_q$ of the base-$q$ digit-sum function $s_q$ satisfies $s_q^{(2)}(n) = \sum_{de = n} s_q(d) \, s_q(e)$, where the sum runs over the pairs $(d, e)$ of positive integers with $de = n$ (there are none for $n = 0$, and then both sides are $0$).

results.title: Delange's function
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: For a natural number $q$, Delange's function in base $q$ is the function of a real number $x$ given by $g(x) = \int_0^x \left(\lfloor q t \rfloor - q \lfloor t \rfloor - \frac{q - 1}{2}\right) dt$, where $\lfloor \cdot \rfloor$ is the floor function.

results.title: Delange's series

results.title: Trollope–Delange fluctuation
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: Let $q$ be a natural number and let $h$ be Delange's series in base $q$. The Trollope–Delange fluctuation in base $q$ is the function of a real number $x$ given by $F(x) = \frac{q - 1}{2}(1 + \lfloor x \rfloor - x) + q^{1 + \lfloor x \rfloor - x}\, h(q^{x - \lfloor x \rfloor - 1})$, where $\lfloor x \rfloor$ is the floor of $x$.

results.title: Periodicity of the Trollope–Delange fluctuation
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: For every natural number $q$ and every real number $x$, the Trollope–Delange fluctuation $F$ in base $q$ satisfies $F(x + 1) = F(x)$.

results.title: Trollope–Delange remainder
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: Let $q$ be a natural number, write $s_q(n)$ for the sum of the base-$q$ digits of a natural number $n$ (with $s_q(n) = n$ when $q \le 1$), and let $h$ be Delange's series in base $q$. For a real number $x$, let $n_x$ be the floor of $x$ when $x \ge 0$ and $n_x = 0$ when $x < 0$. The remainder of the Trollope–Delange formula is $J(x) = (1 + n_x - x)\, s_q(n_x) - h(x)$.

results.summary: For every natural number $n$, the list of pairs $(i, j)$ of natural numbers with $i < j < n$, in encoding order ($i$ ascending and, for each $i$, $j$ descending from $n - 1$ to $i + 1$), contains no pair twice.

results.title: Pair bits are read off by position
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $n$ be a natural number, and let the pair list of $n$ be the list of pairs $(i, j)$ with $i < j < n$ in encoding order. Let $b$ be a list of bits whose length equals the length of the pair list of $n$. For all $i < j < n$, the bit of the pair $(i, j)$ in $b$ is the entry of $b$ at the position of $(i, j)$ in the pair list of $n$.

results.title: Pair bits computed by a function
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $n$ be a natural number, let $f$ be a function from pairs of natural numbers to bits, and let $b$ be the list obtained by applying $f$ to each entry of the pair list of $n$ (the pairs $(i, j)$ with $i < j < n$ in encoding order). Then for all $i < j < n$, the bit of the pair $(i, j)$ in $b$ is $f(i, j)$.

results.title: Complementing the pair bits complements the graph
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $n \in \mathbb{N}$ and let $b$ be a list of bits whose length is the number of pairs $(i, j)$ with $i < j < n$. Then the graph on $\{0, \dots, n-1\}$ read off the list obtained by negating every bit of $b$ is the complement of the graph on $\{0, \dots, n-1\}$ read off $b$.

results.title: Correctness of the complementing map from CLIQUE to INDEPENDENT-SET
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: For every bit string $x$, CLIQUE accepts $x$ if and only if INDEPENDENT-SET accepts the image of $x$ under the complementing map from CLIQUE to INDEPENDENT-SET instances.

results.title: Independent sets and vertex covers of complementary sizes
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $G$ be a simple graph whose vertices are $0, 1, \dots, n - 1$, and let $k \le n$. Then $G$ has an independent set of exactly $k$ vertices if and only if $G$ has a vertex cover of exactly $n - k$ vertices.

results.title: Membership in the literal occurrences of a CNF formula
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $\varphi$ be a CNF formula with clauses $C_0, \dots, C_{m-1}$, let $i$ and $x$ be natural numbers and let $b$ be a Boolean. The triple $(i, x, b)$ belongs to the list of literal occurrences of $\varphi$ if and only if $i < m$ and the literal $(x, b)$ belongs to $C_i$.

results.caption: Theorem

In Karp's graph of $\varphi$, the graph on $\{0, \dots, m-1\}$ read off the clique pair bits of $\varphi$, vertices $i$ and $j$ are adjacent if and only if $i \ne j$ and the occurrences $o_i$ and $o_j$ are adjacent, that is, they lie in different clauses and are not…

results.title: Karp's reduction from SAT to CLIQUE is correct
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: A CNF formula $\varphi$ with $m$ clauses is satisfiable if and only if Karp's graph of $\varphi$ has a clique of exactly $m$ vertices. Karp's graph has one vertex for each literal occurrence of $\varphi$, and two occurrences are adjacent when they lie in different clauses and are not complementary.

results.title: Modes of the clique verifier
results.caption: Inductive
results.summary: A mode is one of three values, clique, independent set and vertex cover, naming the three graph problems CLIQUE, INDEPENDENT-SET and VERTEX-COVER that share one NP verifier.

results.title: Pair condition of the clique verifier

results.title: Vertex pairs in encoding order for one more vertex
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: For a natural number $m$, write $P(m)$ for the list of pairs $(i, j)$ of natural numbers with $i < j < m$, ordered by $i$ ascending and, for each $i$, by $j$ descending. results.title: Chosen-flag pairs

results.title: Reading a list at every index
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: For every list $s$ of Booleans of length $\ell$, reading $s$ at the indices $0, 1, \dots, \ell - 1$ in turn (with default value false) gives back $s$.

results.title: The row-by-row check is the pairwise check
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: For every mode $m$ and all lists of bits $s$ and $b$, the row-by-row check of $s$ against $b$ holds if and only if $b$ has exactly one bit per pair $i < j < |s|$ and, listing these pairs in encoding order (rows $i$ ascending, within a row $j$ descending), the $t$-th pair $(i, j)$ and the $t$-th bit $b_t$ satisfy the pair condition $\mathrm{ok}_m(b_t, s_i, s_j)$ for every $t$.

results.title: The verifier as a row-by-row check
results.caption: Theorem

Suppose that $x$ decodes to $(k, n, \mathit{bits})$, that $w$ has at least $n$ bits, and that exactly $k$ of the first $n$ bits of $w$ are set. Then the verifier for mode $m$ on input $x$ and witness $w$ returns the same value as the row-by-row check for mode $m$ of the first $n$ bits of $w$ against the pair bits $\mathit{bits}$.

results.title: Lookup in a list of pairs with distinct keys
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $l$ be a list of pairs whose keys lie in a type with a lawful Boolean equality and are pairwise distinct. If $(a, b)$ occurs in $l$, then looking up the key $a$ in $l$ returns $b$.

results.title: Counting the set bits of a list built from a function

results.title: Symmetric relations on increasing pairs
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $n$ be a natural number and $R$ a relation on $\{0, \dots, n-1\}$ such that $R(i, j)$ implies $R(j, i)$. Then $R(i, j)$ holds for all $i \ne j$ if and only if $R(i, j)$ holds for all $i < j$.

results.title: Cliques of the graph given by pair bits
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: For natural numbers $n$ and $k$ and a list of bits $b$, the graph on the vertices $0, \dots, n-1$ read off $b$ has a clique of exactly $k$ vertices if and only if there is a set $s$ of exactly $k$ of these vertices meeting the clique-mode pair condition on every pair $i < j$: whenever $i$ and $j$ both lie in $s$, the bit of the pair $\{i, j\}$ in $b$ is set.

results.title: Independent sets of the graph given by pair bits
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: For natural numbers $n$ and $k$ and a list of bits $b$, the graph on the vertices $0, \dots, n-1$ read off $b$ has an independent set of exactly $k$ vertices if and only if there is a set $s$ of exactly $k$ of these vertices meeting the independent-set-mode pair condition on every pair $i < j$: whenever $i$ and $j$ both lie in $s$, the bit of the pair $\{i, j\}$ in $b$ is not set.

results.title: Vertex covers of the graph given by pair bits
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: For natural numbers $n$ and $k$ and a list of bits $b$, the graph on the vertices $0, \dots, n-1$ read off $b$ has a vertex cover of exactly $k$ vertices if and only if there is a set $s$ of exactly $k$ of these vertices meeting the cover-mode pair condition on every pair $i < j$: whenever the bit of the pair $\{i, j\}$ in $b$ is set, $i$ or $j$ lies in $s$.

results.title: CLIQUE is verified with witnesses no longer than the input
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: For every bit string $x$, $x$ is in CLIQUE if and only if there is a bit string $w$ of length at most the length of $x$ such that the shared CLIQUE / INDEPENDENT-SET / VERTEX-COVER verifier, run in clique mode, accepts the input $x$ with witness $w$.

results.title: INDEPENDENT-SET is verified with witnesses no longer than the input
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: For every bit string $x$, $x$ is in INDEPENDENT-SET if and only if there is a bit string $w$ of length at most the length of $x$ such that the shared CLIQUE / INDEPENDENT-SET / VERTEX-COVER verifier, run in independent-set mode, accepts the input $x$ with witness $w$.

results.title: VERTEX-COVER is verified by the clique verifier in cover mode
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: A bit string $x$ is in VERTEX-COVER if and only if there is a bit string $w$, no longer than $x$, such that the clique-family verifier in vertex-cover mode accepts $x$ with witness $w$.

results.title: Stacks of the CLIQUE verifier

results.title: Labels of the CLIQUE verifier

results.title: Karp adjacency of two literals
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: For literals $l = (x, p)$ and $l' = (x', q)$, each a variable $x, x' \in \mathbb{N}$ with a polarity $p, q \in \{\mathrm{true}, \mathrm{false}\}$, the adjacency bit of $l$ and $l'$ is false when they are complementary, that is $x = x'$ and $p \ne q$, and true otherwise. results.title: The halting problem is undecidable by multi-stack machines
results.caption: Theorem

results.title: The halting problem is recognizable by multi-stack machines

results.title: The halting problem is not co-recognizable by multi-stack machines

results.title: Some multi-stack machine has an undecidable halting set
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: There is a multi-stack machine $M$, with a bijection between its input alphabet and the Booleans, such that no multi-stack machine decides, for $n \in \mathbb{N}$, whether $M$ halts when started on the binary representation of $n$ (written in $M$'s input alphabet through the bijection).

results.title: Rice's theorem for multi-stack machines
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $C$ be a set of partial functions $\mathbb{N} \to \mathbb{N}$. If a multi-stack machine decides, for each partial recursive code, whether the function the code computes lies in $C$, then for all partial recursive functions $f$ and $g$, $f \in C$ implies $g \in C$.

results.title: Decidability transfers along mapping reductions
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $p$ and $q$ be predicates on primitive recursively encodable types $\alpha$ and $\beta$. If $p$ is many-one reducible to $q$ and $q$ is decidable by a multi-stack machine, then $p$ is decidable by a multi-stack machine.

results.title: Recognizability transfers along mapping reductions
results.caption: Theorem

results.title: Rice's theorem for partial recursive codes
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $C$ be a set of partial functions $\mathbb{N} \rightharpoonup \mathbb{N}$, and suppose there are partial recursive functions $f \in C$ and $g \notin C$. Then the property of a partial recursive code $c$ that the partial function computed by $c$ belongs to $C$ is not decidable by a multi-stack Turing machine.

results.title: Rice's theorem for languages
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $P$ be a set of subsets of $\mathbb{N}$, and suppose there are partial recursive codes $c_1$ and $c_2$ such that the domain of $c_1$ (the set of inputs on which it halts) belongs to $P$ and the domain of $c_2$ does not. Then the property of a partial recursive code $c$ that the domain of $c$ belongs to $P$ is not decidable by a multi-stack Turing machine.

results.title: Acceptance by a code

results.title: Halting of a code on an input

results.title: Acceptance reduces to halting

results.title: The description relation is recognizable
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $U$ be the universal description method. The set of pairs $(x, p)$ of binary strings such that $U(p)$ is defined and equal to $x$ is recursively enumerable (recognizable).

results.title: Kolmogorov complexity is upper semicomputable
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $K$ denote Kolmogorov complexity. The set of pairs $(x, n)$ of a binary string $x$ and a natural number $n$ with $K(x) \le n$ is recursively enumerable (recognizable).

results.title: A partial recursive map raises complexity by at most a constant
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $K$ denote Kolmogorov complexity and let $f$ be a partial recursive function from binary strings to binary strings. Then there is a natural number $c$ such that $K(y) \le K(x) + c$ for all binary strings $x$ and $y$ such that $f(x)$ is defined and equal to $y$.

results.title: Shortest descriptions are incompressible
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $U$ be the universal description method, $K$ Kolmogorov complexity, and $|p|$ the length of a binary string $p$. There is a natural number $b$ such that for all binary strings $x$ and $p$, if $p$ is a shortest description of $x$, that is, $U(p)$ is defined and equal to $x$ and $|p| = K(x)$, then $|p| \le K(p) + b$.

results.title: Chaitin's incompleteness theorem
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $K$ denote Kolmogorov complexity, and let $S$ be a recursively enumerable (recognizable) set of pairs $(x, n)$ of a binary string $x$ and a natural number $n$ such that $n \le K(x)$ for every $(x, n) \in S$. Then there is a natural number $B$ with $n \le B$ for every $(x, n) \in S$.

results.title: A computable lower bound of Kolmogorov complexity is bounded
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $K$ denote Kolmogorov complexity. If $f$ is a computable function from binary strings to natural numbers with $f(x) \le K(x)$ for every binary string $x$, then there is a natural number $B$ with $f(x) \le B$ for every binary string $x$.

results.title: Kolmogorov complexity is not lower semicomputable
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $K$ denote Kolmogorov complexity. The set of pairs $(x, n)$ of a binary string $x$ and a natural number $n$ with $n \le K(x)$ is not recursively enumerable (recognizable).

results.title: No recognizable set with arbitrarily long members consists of incompressible strings
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $K$ denote Kolmogorov complexity and $|x|$ the length of a binary string $x$. There is no recursively enumerable (recognizable) set $S$ of binary strings such that for every natural number $n$ some $x \in S$ has $|x| \ge n$, and every $x \in S$ satisfies $|x| \le K(x)$.

results.title: The incompressible strings are not recognizable
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $K$ denote Kolmogorov complexity and $|x|$ the length of a binary string $x$. The set of incompressible binary strings, that is, of binary strings $x$ with $|x| \le K(x)$, is not recursively enumerable (recognizable).

results.title: The incompressible strings are not decidable
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $K$ denote Kolmogorov complexity and $|x|$ the length of a binary string $x$. The set of incompressible binary strings, that is, of binary strings $x$ with $|x| \le K(x)$, is not decidable.
